summary: Friedrich Carl Andreas worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic studies. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1867-1868) and held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1887-1903) and the University of Göttingen (~1903-1930).

Friedrich Christian Diez was a linguist who studied at the University of Giessen under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1811-1813) and at the University of Göttingen (~1813-1818). He held a post at the University of Bonn (~1823-1876).

Friedrich Creuzer worked in religious studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied at the Universities of Tübingen (~1789-1791) and Jena (~1791-1794), and held posts at Marburg (~1800-1804), Heidelberg (~1804-1845), and Leiden (1809).

Friedrich Delitzsch specialized in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig under Fleischer, Brockhaus, Curtius, and Windisch (~1868-1873) and in Berlin (~1871-1872). He held posts at the Universities of Breslau (~1893-1899) and Berlin (~1899-1920).
Friedrich Ernst August Krause worked in sinology and religious studies. He studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1900-1903) and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1923-1942).

Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Giessen (~1801-1803), where he later held a post (~1809-1816), followed by posts at Göttingen (~1816-1819) and Bonn (~1819-1859).

Friedrich Haag worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, as well as at Göttingen and Berlin. His academic posts included Dozent at Zurich (1873-1884) and professor of classical philology at Bern (1887; 1891-1906).

Friedrich Heiler was a religious studies scholar who completed his dissertation at the University of Munich (~1912-1917). He held teaching assignments at Munich in 1918 and served as Leiter at the University of Marburg beginning in 1920.

Friedrich Hirth worked in sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald, and served in the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870-1897) before becoming Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University in 1902.

Friedrich Karl Theodor Zarncke worked in linguistics. He studied at Rostock and Leipzig, where he learned under Gottfried Hermann and Moriz Haupt. At Leipzig University, he served as Privatdozent (1852) and Rektor (1869-1882).
Friedrich Kurschat was a linguist who studied at the University of Königsberg (~1834-1840) and later held an academic post there (~1840-1883).
Friedrich Leo was a linguist who studied at Bonn under Hermann Usener and at Göttingen. He held posts at Bonn, Kiel, Rostock, Strasbourg, and the University of Göttingen (1889-1914).

Friedrich Majer specialized in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Jena (~1790-1794) and under Johann Gottfried von Herder (~1798-1803), serving as a Privatdozent at Jena (~1799-1802).

Friedrich Max Müller worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Paris under Brockhaus, Bopp, Schelling, and Burnouf, and under Wilson. His main posts included professorships at the University of Oxford from 1854.

Friedrich Müller worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna, under Anton Boller, and at Göttingen and Tübingen. He held posts at the Vienna University Library, Austrian National Library, and University of Vienna (1858-1898).

Friedrich Nietzsche worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at the University of Bonn and Leipzig University under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and held a faculty post at the University of Basel (1869-1878).

Friedrich Otto Schrader specialized in Indology and religious studies. He earned a doctorate from the University of Strasbourg (~1899-1902), served as Leiter of the Adyar Library (1905-1916), and was Professor of Indology at Kiel University from 1921.

Friedrich Rückert worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg, and under Bopp and von Hammer-Purgstall. He held posts at Jena (1811), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1826), and Berlin (1841-1849).

Friedrich Schleiermacher worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1787-1790), where he later held a post (~1804-1807), before holding a chair at the University of Berlin (~1810-1834).
Friedrich Schrader was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He completed his dissertation under Richard Pischel at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1885-1889).
